summary.text: 不 is the common Chinese negative word “not.” It is attested as a negative particle in oracle-bone inscriptions, though the graph’s original pictured subject remains disputed.

formation.text: 不 is analyzed as a whole-graph pictograph, but its subject is unresolved. Proposals include plant roots or a germ and a flower calyx; a later dictionary explanation depicts a bird flying upward toward the sky. No separate sound component is supported.

components.text: The graph is treated as one whole picture, not as established separate parts. Proposed subjects are roots or a germ, a calyx, and—in a later dictionary account—a bird rising toward a line for the sky.

history.text: The oracle-style and seal-style forms shown are modern redrawings, not ancient artifacts. They represent different script traditions; neither establishes the graph’s original subject or a sequence of graphic changes. Oracle-bone inscriptions document early negative use, while the seal-style form reflects the transmitted dictionary tradition.

uncertainties.text: The original referent remains disputed among roots or a germ, a calyx, and the later bird explanation. One proposed account is that the graph was reused for negation because the old name of its pictured subject sounded similarly; neither that name nor the sound match is established. Negative use is broadly assigned to oracle-bone inscriptions of the 14th–11th centuries BCE, without a specific occurrence date.
No independent phonetic component or component-to-character sound comparison is supported. Reconstructions of the negative word do not establish how any proposed pictured subject was pronounced.

senses.text: 不 is attested as a negative particle in oracle-bone inscriptions. The corpus is dated broadly; no specific occurrence is dated here.

senses.period: Later Archaic Chinese; examples cited from the Analects and Xunzi
senses.text: 不 is used as a general verbal negative in later Archaic Chinese. The intervening development from its earlier particle use is not traced in detail.

senses.period: Modern Chinese; usage varies by language and dialect
senses.text: 不 commonly expresses negation, including as a negative prefix; its distribution varies across modern varieties.

developments.text: Early particle use and later general verbal negation are both documented, but the intervening development is not traced in detail.
Modern negation is documented, but a continuous chronology from Archaic usage to modern distributions is not established.

limitations.text: No earliest attestation of a literal root, germ, calyx, or bird meaning, or a dated path from any proposed picture to negation, is established.
Early negative use is assigned broadly to the oracle-bone corpus; a particular inscription date and a full chronology of later uses are unavailable.

overview.text: 不 means “not” and appears as a negative particle in oracle-bone inscriptions. One proposal is that its picture was reused because the pictured subject’s old name sounded like “not”; that name and sound match are unestablished.

components.text: Treat 不 as one proposed picture: interpretations include roots or a germ, a calyx, and a later account of a bird rising toward the sky.
